issues.description: _shutdown_telemetry rips all LoggingHandler instances off the root logger, mutating global state it doesn't own.
issues.detail: The shutdown path walks the root logger and removes every LoggingHandler, including any OTLP handler installed by user code or other subsystems. This violates the function's stated contract and breaks embedding/multi-job scenarios. Scope removal to the handler this module installed, or track it explicitly by reference.

issues.description: _flush_early_log_buffer picks an OTLP LoggingHandler by isinstance walk instead of holding the handler it created.
issues.detail: The replay path imports LoggingHandler and grabs the first root-logger match, which may be a handler from another subsystem that eats the replay while the real OTLP handler is skipped. This also leaks telemetry implementation details through the JobContext boundary. Expose a replay(records) operation in the telemetry module and hold the created handler reference.

issues.description: _BufferingHandler.buffer is unbounded with no size cap or drop policy.
issues.detail: If a job hangs before session.start() under high log volume, the buffer grows without limit and can OOM the worker. State an explicit invariant (max records, ring buffer, or drop-oldest) and enforce it in emit(), logging a one-line warning on drop. A crash-log feature must not become a memory-exhaustion vector.

issues.description: PR bundles three unrelated changes: crash-log upload, a worker.py race fix, and makefile parallelism removal.
issues.detail: Reordering _queue_msg vs pending_assignments is a real race fix; dropping -n auto and test_plugin_google_stt.py is test-infra surgery; neither belongs in a patch titled 'upload logs to server even when session fails to start.' Split into separate commits so bisect, revert, and per-contract review work cleanly.

issues.description: init_recording is overloaded — _on_cleanup invokes it with synthetic options to opportunistically flush crash logs.
issues.detail: init_recording's precondition (not yet initialized AND cloud URL) and single postcondition are now muddied by a cleanup-path call with audio/traces/transcript all false. Introduce a dedicated _ensure_crash_log_pipeline() (or split init_recording from teardown of buffering) so each contract is visible and preconditions don't drift.

issues.description: Dropping pytest-xdist (-n auto) from unit-tests serializes CI without justification in the diff.
issues.detail: Removing parallelism slows the suite for everyone. If test_plugin_google_stt.py was flaky under xdist, document it in the commit message and quarantine that test rather than punishing the whole suite. As written it reads like a local workaround that escaped into main.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the underlying idea — buffer logs early, flush through OTLP once recording initializes, force-resolve shutdown on early crash — is the right shape and addresses a real gap. Execution leaks telemetry internals across module boundaries: shutdown mutates the root logger globally, and the replay path locates the OTLP handler by isinstance walk rather than holding the reference it created. The buffer is unbounded, init_recording has been overloaded for cleanup-path crash-log flushing, and the patch bundles a worker.py race fix and makefile parallelism removal that belong in separate commits. NEEDS-WORK: tighten the telemetry contract, bound the buffer, and split the patch.
